title: Favorite clarinet and trombone players
summary: Zanco likes Alphonse Picou, Albert Burbank and George Lewis, and for trombone Archie Rogers, Bob Havens and Jim Robinson.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Oh, I tell you, when it gets, uh, when it gets on the subject of jazz, I could, I could talk on and on and on. But if I didn't have to run off and go put out flyers this afternoon, I would stay here all day.
I thought of one thing I could ask you. Who some of your favorite clarinet players were, for example.

What are you saying? Uh, I liked, uh, Alphonse Piku. I liked, uh, I liked what, I liked Albert Burbank. Uh, George Lewis. I think I like them all. I mean, if the guys can play, you can't help them like them. You gotta appreciate what they're doing, you know. I just like them all. Anybody that plays jazz, I like, you know, I will listen to.

Trombone? Uh, well, I'll have to say, uh, Archie Rogers, as far as I'm concerned, is one of the best in the city. I mean, maybe a lot of other people don't know that or have never heard him play. But personally, I think he's one of the best. Then, uh, Bob Havens is good. Bob Havens, uh, plays with Hurts Grove. He's good. Then, uh, I like Jim Robinson. I could go on, I could think of quite a few of them, but offhand, you know.
I just want you offhand. Yeah. I prefer to have that, you know, kind of.
